title: Check yourself: Install, the working loop and permission modes

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A developer wants Claude to study a repository and show a written draft before any file on disk changes. Which start fits?

options.text: The `default` mode, which asks about each action one by one
options.says: Ruled out because the table lists `default` (Manual) for "Reviewing every action yourself", so it prompts action by action and no draft comes first.

options.text: The `acceptEdits` mode, which writes edits without asking
options.says: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands" without asking, so edits land on disk at once.
The page says "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve", and `claude --permission-mode plan` starts there.

options.text: The `dontAsk` mode, which denies whatever would prompt
options.says: Ruled out because `dontAsk` runs "Reads and pre-approved tools; anything that would prompt is denied", so it denies and shows no draft.

origin.section: The loop: explore, plan, code, commit

questions.stem: A repository's shared settings file sets the starting permission mode to `bypassPermissions`. What happens when a teammate opens it?

options.text: The session starts in auto mode for every teammate who opens it
options.says: Ruled out because that is exactly what the rule prevents, since "the value doesn't take effect".

options.text: The value is ignored, and each edit and command asks first
options.says: The page says a `"bypassPermissions"` set in those two files "doesn't take effect either, and the session starts in Manual mode".

options.text: The session starts in plan mode until the file is approved
options.says: Ruled out because the page names Manual mode and not plan mode: "the session starts in Manual mode".

options.text: Every teammate is asked once to accept the project file's mode
options.says: Ruled out because "The other values apply from any settings file", and these two are the exceptions, so no prompt is shown.

questions.stem: Rules given early in a long conversation stop being followed. Where should a rule that must always apply be kept?

options.text: In a `/compact` summary, which condenses the thread so far
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost", so a summary is where they are lost.

options.text: In a `/clear` command, which starts fresh on a new task
options.says: Ruled out because `/clear` is described as one that "starts fresh on a new task while keeping project memory", so the rules must already be in the memory file.

options.text: In a rewind checkpoint, which snapshots files before each edit
options.says: Ruled out because checkpoints "only cover file changes", so a checkpoint holds files and not rules.

options.text: In `CLAUDE.md`, which sits outside the running chat
options.says: The page says "Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md", because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost."
